dataset.sellerDistribution: 100 sellers interleaved in ascending generated row order

method.statement: EXPLAIN (ANALYZE, BUFFERS, WAL, SETTINGS, FORMAT JSON) INSERT INTO target SELECT * FROM seed
method.order: baseline/candidate interleaved; warm seed table; target tables truncated between runs
method.baselineIndexes: primary key, seller unique, allocation ordinal unique
method.docker: disposable PostgreSQL container; no volume or host port; image defaults

limitations: One synthetic data shape and one PostgreSQL container; execution-time ranges overlap, although all five paired time deltas were positive.
The insert test isolates allocation row/index maintenance; it omits foreign-key checks, parent-table writes, application transaction overhead, and commit latency.
The 1% seller read selectivity and full-period statement path come from the separate EXP-018 read A/B; actual production read/write frequency is unknown.
The break-even ratio excludes WAL retention, storage, cache, vacuum, and concurrent-load costs.
The 8,264 KiB insert-grown index differs from the 4,880 KiB bulk-built index in the read A/B; the former reflects this fixture's incremental insert order, not a universal size per row.
The production migration duration and write-blocking impact of building the candidate index are unmeasured.
